newsitem.title: UK: Gossard says sexy new ads follow 1996 controversy.
newsitem.headline: Gossard says sexy new ads follow 1996 controversy.

text.p: A lingerie manufacturer that was blasted by consumers last year for sexual imagery in its advertising said on Friday it was launching a big poster campaign with "raunchy, humerous" headlines.

In 1996 more than 300 shoppers complained to Britain's advertising regulator when Gossard Glossies launched poster ads showing a woman in underwear lying on the grass, with the caption "Who said a woman can't get pleasure from something soft".
The Advertising Standards Authority said in its annual report in April the Gossard campaign "created a storm of controversy" when the ASA decided not to ban the posters.

But the ASA, which has a self-regulatory role over non-broadcast advertising, did warn advertisers at the time "to be more sensitive to public opinion when portraying women, especially in poster campaigns".
Gossard said on Friday its new ad campaign, which, like the 1996 campaign, was created by Abbott Mead Vickers BBDO agency, would appear on 1,000 billboards on May 15.
Gossard is owned by Courtaulds Textiles Plc, the British clothing group.
